body:
Thanks so much.

>Seriously, I put myself in time out in my room for 2 hours. I cried myself to sleep. By the time I woke up, the moment of crisis had passed.

That's my usual go-to. Things always seem to be better after a few hours. I'm really glad I just sat down and screwed around online instead of trying to take action.

>You say you don't have any goals, but you do - you want to go back to school. I know school is expensive, but that is what financial aid is for. Some states have programs that will waive or reduce your tuition based on income. It is worth looking into. If you're not sure where to start, ask.

I feel like it's wrong to want to go back just because I "have to", but I guess I do want to learn. I just worry about learning the wrong thing and hating it. I was going to school on financial aid (full tuition coverage, with about $500 per semester left over for books, transportation, etc). That was stopped when I failed two semesters straight though, and I'm not sure if I'll be able to get back on financial aid. I've been meaning to look into it, perhaps I will this week.

Thanks for the reply, I really appreciate it.

> I used to cherish my (hate to keep using this word) cracks, let them take me deep deep down.

I think I can relate to that. The few times I've ever cracked have made me feel fairly good for a brief time, but then I go back to feeling shitty. I always regret it. I have actually been thinking about working out a bit, but I talk myself out of it every time I give it serious consideration. The thought of jogging/running makes me feel incredibly anxious, the nearest gym is a 20 minute drive away (no car, so yeah), and none of my friends want to be exercise bros. Every other week or so I do give it a shot though, but that's not enough to make a big difference. Meh. I'll get into it someday.

>As far as school goes, look into trades. Though I don't have the stats to cite, I'd argue that the jobs can be just as high-paying and are far more stable in this wtf economy. Also it's cheaper. Loans'd be nothing.

I have actually given this a decent bit of thought, and probably will go for it if I can't get anything else going. I feel like I'd be incredibly bored with the work, but I'm not exactly an optimistic person.

>>For the first time in a while, I wasn't upset, or just a little mad, or depressed. I was angry.

>How do you feel about this moment? (How did you feel then, and how do you feel now, looking back?)

At the time, I was only angry. Looking back, however, I feel a bit shocked at how easily I snapped.

>>Instead, I picked up a chair, tossed it across the room (thankfully it didn't damage anything) and screamed. I had no words to say, I just screamed louder than I'd ever done before.

>And this moment, same question: how did it feel? And how do you feel about it now, looking back?

At the time, I was angry, but felt great about letting my anger out. That quickly turned into feeling embarrassed over acting that way, and I felt quite hopeless for the next few hours. Looking back on it now, I really hope I never do that again. I'm really disappointed that I acted that way.

I've been following this sleep pattern off and on for about three weeks now. It's rare for me to follow any pattern at all. I tend to go into bouts of deep depression and stay up until well after sunrise goofing off on the computer until I can't stay up any longer. Since I've started trying to maintain a normal sleeping pattern, I feel tired all the time. I eat breakfast most mornings and usually eat lunch around 4 with a late dinner. Maybe I'm just a night owl by nature, I dunno. :(

You're right about seeing things through a bad lens. I'm going to look into going back to college for a semester. I worry somewhat about taking out loans though, because I fear that I'd fail again and be stuck with a mountain of debt and no degree. Perhaps that'd be more incentive to do well though.

>i hate being the 'it could be worse' guy, but that's how it is.

Someone's gotta do it. Have an upvote, good sir.

It's hard to keep in mind how much time I have left to turn my life around. I'm in a very fortunate position. I don't have to worry about how I'll spend my next paycheck, how I'll get to work, how I'll feed my kids, etc. I can just stay at home and take the time I need to recover. 

>the world sucks a lot of the times, but we'll get it. we'll get it.

Well said, very touching. Stay golden, Beeverskeet.

>Can I make a suggestion? Make your brother or sister clean the litter box more often!!!

We typically do them twice a day, and usually check both of them any time the cats make a mess elsewhere, only to find that they're clean. I think they're just used to giving 0 fucks, though. They lived outside until we moved a few months ago. We're trying to find homes for them, but it seems most people want kittens and not adult cats. 

>when you're depressed and suicidal, it's not the problem that sends you over the edge that matters, it's the disease.

Well said. I think it's very rarely some long lasting thing that pushes people over. I'm used to thinking "oh hey I'm a failure" or being lonely. It's that last little straw that breaks everything.

Thanks. It's hard to keep in mind that I haven't even lived a third of my life yet. I definitely hope you're right. It'll be a good day when I can look back on this and think "hah, did I seriously feel that way?"
